content.text: To improve application performance and reduce unnecessary database hits, InfyGo integrates Redis caching with its Spring Boot application. Redis stores previously retrieved data, enabling subsequent requests to be served from the cache.

items: How to create a Spring Boot app with caching enabled
Integration of Redis as the cache provider
Real-time user registration example using cache

content.text: A technique to store copies of frequently accessed data in a temporary storage (cache), reducing data retrieval time and load on backend systems.
An in-memory data store that supports various data structures like strings, lists, sets, and is commonly used as a cache, message broker, or database.
Spring Boot provides declarative caching using annotations such as @Cacheable, @CachePut, and @CacheEvict.
Use Spring Initializr to create the project with:

content.text: Note: @Cacheable only works when the method is called externally (i.e., not through self-invocation).

  mvc:
    view:
      prefix: /WEB-INF/pages/
      suffix: .jsp
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/db_irs
    username: root
    password: root
  cache:
    type: redis
  redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379

server:
  servlet:
    context-path: /InfyGoBoot
  port: 4343

  file: Errorlog.log

    root: warn
    com.infoys.ars: error

sections.heading: Spring Boot vs Non-Spring Boot Caching

items: Caching helps improve application performance and scalability.
Redis is a high-performance, in-memory data store commonly used with Spring Boot.
Spring Boot makes caching integration simple using annotations and auto-configuration.
Minimal code changes with significant performance gains.
